summary: Axios impersonation pulling unrelated dependencies into the install tree
details: Package published under the `@qwedqwed` scope mimics the popular `axios` HTTP client: dist/node/axios.cjs is a verbatim copy of upstream axios, and package.json forges upstream provenance (author `Matt Zabriskie`, repository `github.com/axios/axios`, homepage `axios-http.com`) despite the unrelated scope. On top of axios's normal dependencies, package.json declares two extra dependencies — `@caspianph/storyteller@^1.0.0` and `math@^0.0.3` — that are not part of upstream axios. Installing or requiring this package therefore silently pulls those unrelated packages into node_modules, where their code runs at require time. The library code itself contains no exfil/RCE primitive; the impersonation and forged metadata exist solely to lower a developer's guard so the injected transitives are accepted. Whether the injected deps are themselves malicious must be evaluated separately, but the delivery shape (axios-clone lure + scope mismatch + forged author/repo + two undeclared extra deps) is namespace-abuse.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
